reels.creator: fit.khurana
reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (24g P, 480 Cals)

Ingredients

🧆 110g @freshconindia boiled chickpeas
🥣 80g Skyr (high protein yogurt)
🥑 2 tbsp avocado
🧅 1 tbsp chopped onion
🥒 ½ cucumber ribbons
🍅 2 tomato slices 
🌶️ 1 tsp peri peri masala
🌶️ 1 tbsp Sriracha sauce
🫒 1–2 oil sprays
🌯 1 whole-wheat tortilla 
🧂 Salt & black pepper, to taste
🥬 Lettuce

How to Make –

1. Lightly spray a non-stick pan with oil and add the half  boiled chickpeas. 
2. Add 1 tsp peri peri masala and roast the chickpeas for around 5–6 minutes until they are properly coated and crunchy. 
3. Take the remaining boiled chickpeas and add them to a bowl along with Skyr, avocado and onion. 
4. Add around 1 tbsp Sriracha, a little salt and black pepper, and mash everything together until you get a creamy dressing. 
6. Warm the whole-wheat tortilla lightly on the pan. 
7. Add lettuce, spread the creamy chickpea dressing over the tortilla, then add the cucumber ribbons and tomato slices. 🥒🍅
8. Add the crunchy peri peri chickpeas on top and fold or roll the tortilla.

reels.creator: fit.khurana
reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (Serves 6 | ~8g Protein | ~180 Cals)

Ingredients

🥛 1 litre toned milk
🌸 Saffron, soaked in a little water
🌰 4–5 almonds + 4–5 cashews + 4–5 pistachios, chopped
🥛 2 tbsp skimmed milk powder, mixed with a little water
🌾 ¼ cup roasted makhana, powdered
🌾 70g roasted whole makhana
🍬 Zero-calorie sweetener, as per taste
🌹 Rose petals, optional
🥭 Mango or sitaphal pulp, optional

How to Make –

1. Add 1 litre toned milk to a heavy-bottomed kadai and cook on low flame to reduce. 

2. Keep stirring continuously for around 10–15 minutes. This is important because the milk can stick to the bottom if you don’t keep stirring. 🥄

3. Mix 2 tbsp skimmed milk powder with a little water to make a smooth, thin mixture. After the milk has reduced a little, slowly add this mixture to the milk while continuously stirring. 🥛

4. Add the saffron water while the milk is cooking and continue stirring on a low flame. 🌸

5. Roast the makhana until crisp. Take ¼ cup of the roasted makhana and grind it into a fine powder. 🌾

6. Add the makhana powder to the milk and mix well. This will help thicken the milk and give it a creamy texture. 🥣

7. Add the remaining 70g roasted whole makhana along with the chopped almonds, cashews and pistachios. Mix everything well. 

8. Add zero-calorie sweetener as per your taste and continue cooking on a low flame for a few more minutes.

9. Turn off the flame and let it cool. Transfer it to the fridge and chill for a few hours. ❄️

10. Serve chilled. You can optionally add rose petals or fruit pulp of your choice mango or sitaphal both go really well✨

✅Add 1/2 chopped onion, 1 tomato, and lemon juice to a handchopper

✅Blend 100g low fat paneer, 60g greek yogurt, soaked dried red chillies and salt until creamy (Refrigerate for 10 mins) 

Assemble and enjoy✨

reels.creator: fit.khurana
reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (19g Protein | ~360 Cals | ~11g Fibre) - per serve
 
Ingredients - 2 serves
 
🫘 150g yellow moong dal (soaked for 3 hour) 
🌶️ 2 green chillies 
🧄 2 garlic cloves 
🌾 20g rice flour 
🧅 1 tbsp finely chopped onion 
🌿 1 tbsp chopped coriander 
🟤 ½ tsp cumin seeds
🌾 ¼ tsp ajwain
🌶️ ¼ tsp red chilli powder 
🟡 ¼ tsp turmeric 
🌶️ ½ tsp chaat masala 
🧂 Salt to taste 
🥄 ¼ tsp baking soda 
🫒 1 tsp hot oil 
🫒 Oil spray, 2–3 sprays 
 
For the dressing: 
 
🥣 50g Skyr 
🌿 1 tbsp green chutney 
 
How to Make – 
 
1. Soak 150g yellow moong dal for 1 hour. Drain it well. 🫘 
2. Take 100g of the soaked dal along with the green chillies and garlic. Add 2–3 tbsp water little by little and grind into a coarse, thick paste.
3. Transfer the ground mixture to a bowl and whip it well for 1–2 minutes to incorporate air.
4. Add the remaining 50g soaked whole dal, rice flour, coriander, cumin seeds, ajwain, red chilli powder, turmeric, and chaat masala. Mix everything well.
5. Don’t add the salt, baking soda, or onion yet. Keep the batter thick. 
6. Preheat your air fryer to 200°C for 5 minutes. 
7. Once the air fryer is hot, add the chopped onion, salt, ¼ tsp baking soda, and 1 tsp hot oil to the batter. Mix well. 
8. Make small dollops of around 20–25g each.
9. Lightly oil spray the dollops and air fry at 190°C for around 8 minutes. 
11. Flip them and spray with oil again a d air fry at 200°C for another 6–8 minutes, until deep golden and crispy. It’s completely okay if it sticks to the bottom, just scrape, flip and air fry. Mine stuck too but came out beautiful❤️
13. For the dressing, mix 50g Skyr with 1 tbsp green chutney until smooth and creamy.

reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (~8g Protein | ~180 Cals)

Ingredients (1 Serve only - Small cup)

🧈 ½ tbsp ghee
🌰 1–2 cashews + 2–3 almonds, crushed (optional; not included in macros)
🧆 2 tbsp besan
💧 ½ cup boiling water
🍇 3–5 raisins (optional)
🥛 100 ml skimmed milk
🌕 ¼ tsp turmeric
⚫ 2–3 black peppercorns
🍬 Zero-calorie sweetener, as per taste
🪴 Pinch of Elaichi powder 

How to Make

1. Heat ½ tbsp ghee in a pan on low-medium heat. 
2. If using, add the crushed cashews and almonds and lightly roast them in the ghee. 
3. Add 20g besan and roast on low heat, stirring continuously, until it turns golden brown and smells beautifully nutty. 
4. Grind/crush the turmeric and black peppercorns together, add them to the roasted besan along with zero-calorie sweetener mix well. 
5. Add the raisins to boiling water. Then slowly pour in ½ cup boiling water, a little at a time in the besan, while stirring continuously to prevent lumps. 
6. Gradually add 100 ml skimmed milk, continuing to stir. Don’t pour it all in at once!!
7. Cook on low heat for another 4–5 minutes, stirring continuously, until smooth, creamy and properly cooked. 
8. If you prefer a thinner, more drinkable consistency, add a little more hot water.

reels.creator: veronicabahl
reels.caption:
THE CHOCOLATE CAKE THAT’S ACTUALLY BREAKFAST 🍫🥒

I finally decided to make my own after having one of the best zucchini chocolate cakes at Chorus Café in Bombay a couple of weeks ago. That’s where the inspiration for this recipe came from. ❤️

RECIPE ↓

Ingredients:
• 50g rolled oats
• 75g green zucchini, grated
• 2 whole eggs OR 1 whole egg + 4 egg whites
- 1 tea spoon baking powder and half tea spoon baking soda 
• 40g banana
• 40ml almond milk
• 30g cocoa powder
• 30g sugar-free sweetener

METHOD:

Add the oats, grated zucchini, eggs (if using 2 whole eggs), banana, almond milk, cocoa powder and sweetener to a blender. Blend until completely smooth.

If the batter feels too thick, add a little water and blend again. You want it to be smooth, thick but still runny enough to pour.

If you’re using 1 whole egg + 4 egg whites, whisk the egg whites separately until slightly fluffy, then gently fold them into the blended batter.

This makes the cake lighter and airier.

I personally prefer using 2 whole eggs because it makes the cake denser, richer and more mousse-like. 🤌🏼

Grease an oven/air-fryer-safe dish with one spray of olive oil and line with baking paper. Pour in the batter.

BAKE:
200°C for 20 minutes
then 250°C for another 5–10 minutes.

Every oven/air fryer is different, so check it as you go. Insert a fork into the centre — it should come out clean when the cake is cooked through.

TOP IT OFF 🍓🫐

I HIGHLY recommend a mountain of fresh + frozen berries. The tartness cuts through the dense, mousse-y chocolate cake SO well.

Roasted dry fruits also work beautifully if that’s more your thing.

reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (25g Protein | ~440 Cals)

Ingredients

🥒 2 cucumbers
🍚 80g cooked rice
🧆 80g boiled chickpeas
🥑 30g avocado
🥣 120g Skyr
🌶️ 1 tsp chilli oil
🌶️ 1 jalapeño (finely chopped)
🧂 Salt to taste
⚫ A pinch of sesame seeds
🌶️ Sriracha sauce, as required

For the dipping sauce:
🥢 Soy sauce
💧 A little water
🍋 Lemon juice
🍯 A little honey

How to Make –

1. Cut the cucumbers in half lengthwise. Using a small spoon, scoop out the entire inner portion and clean them well to create cucumber boats. 🥒
2. Lightly mash the cooked rice until it becomes slightly sticky. Press and spread the rice evenly inside the cucumber boats. 🍚
3. In a bowl, add the boiled chickpeas, avocado, Skyr, chilli oil, chopped jalapeño, and salt. Mash everything together until you get a creamy mixture. 🧆🥑
4. Spread the chickpea mixture evenly over the rice layer in each cucumber boat. 🥄
5. Sprinkle sesame seeds on top and drizzle with Sriracha. 🌶️✨
6. Cut each cucumber half into 2–3 pieces to make bite-sized boats. 🔪
7. For the dipping sauce, mix soy sauce with a little water, lemon juice, and honey. 🥣🍋
8. Serve the cucumber boats with the dipping sauce on the side, dip, and enjoy! 🥒🍣😋

reels.creator: fit.khurana
reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (40g P, 390 Cals, 9g Fibre)

Ingredients - 

🧆 30 g besan
🧀 100 g High Protein Paneer
🥬 ¾ cup spinach, roughly chopped
🍄 6–7 mushrooms, chopped
🍅 2-3 cherry tomatoes
🧀 ½ cheese slice
🧂 Salt, to taste
🌶️ ½ tsp red chilli flakes
🌿 ½ tsp mixed herbs
⚫ ¼ tsp black pepper
🫒 2-3 Oil sprays 

Method

1. In a bowl, whisk together the besan, salt, black pepper, red chilli flakes, mixed herbs, and enough water to make a smooth, pourable batter (slightly thinner than dosa batter).
2. Heat a non-stick pan and add the chopped mushrooms without any oil. Cook for 2–3 minutes until they release their moisture and turn lightly golden.
3. Add the spinach and cherry tomatoes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, then sauté for another 1–2 minutes. Remove the veggies from the pan and set aside.
4. Lightly spray the pan with oil and pour in the besan batter and spread it into a large omlette (not too thin or it will become crispy).
5. Once the omlette is about halfway cooked evenly grate the High Protein Paneer over the top and gently press it down with a spatula.
6. When the omlette is cooked, place the sautéed vegetables over one half and top them with the cheese slice.
7. Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 2 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
8. Fold the omlette, drizzle with your favourite hot sauce, and enjoy! 🌯🔥

reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (470 Cals, 30g P) 

Ingredients-

🌸Kebabs -
40g Soya Chunks
1/2 Onion
1/2 Cup Corn
1.5 tbsp Rice flour
Masalas - Salt, Pepper, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 ts dhaniya powder, 1/4tsp garam masala, 1/4tsp haldi, 1/2 tsp jeera
1 green chilli
2-3 garlic cloves
1 cube cheese - cut into 4
1tsp ghee
For bread crumbs - Grind 1 slice whole wheat bread

1. Boil soya chunks and squeeze them well until all water is drained out
2. In a pan, add ghee and sauté garlic, chilli and jeera
3. Add onion, corn and sauté until golden brown
4. Add masalas and mix well
5. Blend this along with rice flour and soya chunks
6. Apply ghee on your hands and roll into cutlets while stuffing small cubes of cheese in each cutlet
7. Roll into bread crumbs and pan fry on each side until crispy. (May take 15 mins on med-low flame)

🌸For chutney -
Handful dhaniya
1 tbsp greek yogurt
1-2 walnuts
1/2 green chilli
1 garlic clove
1/2 lemon juice
Salt and pepper

- Blend everything together and its ready!!

reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (💪 35g Protein | 🔥 570 Cals | 🌾 9g Fibre) - Can divide into 2 servings

Ingredients -

🍝 50g Lentil Spaghetti
🧀 120g low fat/toned milk  paneer
🧅 1½ medium onions, thinly sliced
🍄 Mushrooms, sliced
🧄 Garlic, minced
🫒 1 tsp olive oil
🌶️ Chilli oil, to taste
🧀 Cheese grated 1 tbsp
🍬 Zero-calorie sweetener, to taste
🧂 Salt, to taste
⚫ Black pepper, to taste

Toppings

🌿 Fresh basil leaves

How to Make

1️⃣ Boil the spaghetti according to the package instructions. Reserve the pasta water and drain the spaghetti.

2️⃣ Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and cook until lightly browned.

3️⃣ Add a splash of water and continue cooking. Repeat this process 2–3 times until the onions become deeply caramelized.

4️⃣ Add the garlic and mushrooms. Cook for 1–2 minutes, then pour in a splash of the reserved pasta water and let the mushrooms cook until tender.

5️⃣ Season with chilli oil, salt, black pepper, and zero-calorie sweetener.

6️⃣ Blend the low-fat paneer with water until completely smooth. Pour the paneer sauce into the pan with the flame at lowest and mix well.

7️⃣ Add the cooked spaghetti and toss until everything is evenly coated. Add more reserved pasta water if needed to adjust the consistency.

8️⃣ Finish with cheese, garnish with fresh basil leaves, and serve hot.

reels.creator: fit.khurana
reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (💪 30g Protein | 🔥 430 kcal | 🌾 8g Fibre

Ingredients -

🥣 35–40g @thedrchoice High-Protein Muesli - use my code  FITKDC for a discount
🥣 150g high protein greek yoghurt (Skyr)
🍫 1 tbsp cocoa powder
🥜 ½ tbsp peanut butter
🍫 1 tbsp melted 85% dark chocolate
🫐 8-10 Blueberries
🍋 Lemon zest (optional, for the compote)

How to Make

1️⃣ In a bowl, mix the Skyr, cocoa powder, and peanut butter until smooth.

2️⃣ Line a sieve with a clean muslin cloth and transfer the mixture into it. Wrap it tightly and refrigerate for at least 3-4 hours or overnight.

3️⃣ To make the blueberry compote, add the blueberries to a pan with a splash of water. Cook for 5-6 minutes until they become soft and jammy. Optionally add a little lemon zest for freshness. Let it cool.

4️⃣ Unwrap the chilled Skyr and place it on a serving plate.

5️⃣ Pour the melted 85% dark chocolate over the top.

6️⃣ Sprinkle the high-protein muesli around the Skyr.

7️⃣ Finish with the blueberry compote and serve immediately.

Ingredients:

🍉 1 Watermelon
🥥 2 tbsp Coconut Milk

How to Make -

1. Cut the watermelon in half and scoop a hole in the center.

2. Freeze for 24 hours or until completely frozen.

3. Pour chilled coconut milk into the center.

4. Scrape the frozen fruit with a spoon until it turns creamy.

5. Mix well, scoop, and enjoy!

Also works with:

🥭 Mango
🍈 Muskmelon
🌺 Dragon Fruit
🍍 Pineapple

Recipe ⬇️ (35g Protein, 400 Cals)

Ingredients (Makes 2 Toasties)

🍞 2 slices high-protein bread
🥣 150g high-protein yogurt
🥄 1 tbsp cookable protein powder
🥄 1 tbsp custard powder
🍋 Zest of 1 lemon
🥥 1 tbsp grated coconut
✨ A pinch of cinnamon
🍬 Zero-calorie sweetener, to taste
🫐 6–7 frozen blueberries per slice (Pluckk)
🥥 Frozen grated coconut (Pluckk)

Optional Toppings

🥜 Peanut Butter
🍬 Zero-calorie sweetener

How to Make

1️⃣ In a bowl, mix the high-protein yogurt, cookable protein powder, custard powder, lemon zest, grated coconut, cinnamon, and zero-calorie sweetener until smooth.

2️⃣ Gently press the centre of each bread slice with the back of a spoon to create a shallow dent.

3️⃣ Spoon the yogurt mixture onto each slice.

4️⃣ Top with the frozen blueberries.

5️⃣ Air fry at 180°C for 7–8 minutes until golden and the filling is set.

6️⃣ Slice and serve. Optionally drizzle with peanut butter and a little extra zero-calorie sweetener.

Recipe ⬇️ (390 Calories | 24.8g Protein)

Ingredients (Makes 1 Large Wrap)

🌱 120g Firm Tofu
🌽 1 tsp Corn Flour
🌯 3 Urban Platter Rice Papers (22cm)
🥬 Lettuce
🥕 Julienned Carrot
🥬 Shredded Cabbage
🥒 Julienned Cucumber

For the Korean Tofu:

🥢 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
🌶️ 1 tbsp Gochujang
🍯 1 tsp Honey
🍋 Juice of ½ Lemon
🫒 1 tsp Olive Oil
🧂 Salt & Black Pepper
✨ 1 tsp Sesame Seeds

Yogurt Chilli Dressing:

🥣 50g Greek Yogurt
🌶️ 1 tsp Chilli Sauce
💧 Water (to thin)
🧂 Salt to taste

How to Make -

1. Season the tofu with salt, black pepper, and corn flour. Pan-fry it in olive oil until crispy.
2. Add soy sauce, gochujang, honey, and lemon juice to the pan. Toss until the tofu is well coated, then sprinkle over the sesame seeds.
3. In a bowl, mix together the toguet, chilli sauce, water, and salt to make a smooth yogurt dressing.
4. Dip each rice paper in water for a few seconds until soft.
5. Layer the lettuce, cabbage, carrot, cucumber, crispy tofu, and yogurt dressing on the rice papers.
6. Roll tightly and serve with the remaining yogurt dressing on the side.

15 cals dark choc brownie bites for the snacky gals out here. 

before anyone comes for me: 15 cals is MY number because i cut mine into a 9x9 grid. cut yours bigger, cut yours smaller, the math bends to your knife.

anyway. i made brownie bites and they are gooey little reminders that all the good stuff can be made at home. 

the dry team:
100g gluten free plain flour (Yes You Can)
30g Dutch processed cocoa (Ossoro)
1 scoop Func Lab chocolate plant protein (use code ANKITA on website for a discount)
30g sugar free cook & bake 
a little baking soda + a little baking powder
2-3g zero sugar chocolate pudding mix
2 spoons zero sugar Bourn Vita
sift all of that. 

the good stuff:
40g Amul bitter chocolate + 4 Royce discs + 40g Amul light butter. microwave it, then let it come back to room temp before you touch it again. patience.
4 egg whites, whipped to stiff peaks. the airier the better, this is the whole 

putting it together:
fold the egg whites into the dry mix. when it needs moisture, start adding almond milk (i used 137 degrees). measure with your heart. grease your pan with a bit of olive oil. oven preheated to 180 for 10-15 mins.
fold in the whites, fold in the milk, then the cooled chocolate butter mix.
bake 20 mins. skewer test, kill the oven when there are barely any crumbs on the stick.
do NOT rip it out of the pan immediately. let it cool, chop it up, fridge it so the chocolate and butter set into gooey goodness. serve on a cake stand if ur fancy like me. 

enjoy. don’t @ me about the calories.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ or you can. I have done the math too many times.

reels.caption:
Recipe ⬇️ (435 Calories | 24.8g Protein | 7g Fibre)

Ingredients (Makes 1 Serving)

🥣 50g Suji
🥛 100g Skyr
🌱 100g Silken Tofu
🫒 1 tsp Oil
🥜 3-4 Peanuts
🌾 ½ tsp Mustard Seeds (Rai)
🧂 ½ tsp Cumin Seeds (Jeera)
✨ A pinch of Hing
🥄 1 tsp Urad Dal
🍇 3–4 Raisins (optional)
🧅 1 Small Onion, finely chopped
🌶️ Green Chilli, finely chopped
🥕 ½ Carrot, finely chopped
🫛 ¼ Cup Green Peas
🌿 Curry Leaves
🧄 Garlic, finely chopped
🌶️ Red Chilli Powder
💛 Turmeric (Haldi)
🧂 Salt to taste
🍬 Sweetener of choice (optional)
💧 150ml Water

How to Make -

1. Blend the skyr and silken tofu until smooth and keep aside.
2. Heat the oil and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, hing, urad dal, peanuts, and curry leaves. Once fragrant, add the garlic, green chilli, and onion, then sauté until the onion softens.
3. Add the suji and roast it for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
4. Bring 200ml water to a boil with the carrot, green peas, and raisins.
5. Add the boiling water to the roasted suji and mix well.
6. Stir in the skyr and tofu blend along with turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and a little sweetener.
7. Cook on low heat for 4–6 minutes, stirring continuously until the upma reaches a soft and creamy consistency.

Recipe ⬇️ (Serves 2 | Per Serving: 380 kcal | 31g Protein | 5.5g Fibre)

Ingredients - 

🧅 1 large onion, roughly chopped
🍅 3 medium tomatoes, roughly chopped
🧄 4–5 garlic cloves, minced
🌶️ 2 green chillies
🌿 1 bay leaf
🟤 1 tsp cumin seeds
⚫ 4–5 whole black peppercorns
🟢 2 green cardamom
🌰 1 tbsp melon seeds (magaz)
🥦 4–5 cauliflower florets (boiled)
🎃 ¼ cup pumpkin (boiled)
🧀 100g High Protein Paneer (for blending)
🧀 100-120g  High Protein Paneer, cut into cubes/triangles
🥛 50ml low-fat milk
🧂 Salt, to taste
🌶️ Red chilli powder, to taste
💛 Turmeric powder
🌿 Coriander powder
🟤 Cumin powder
✨ Garam masala
🤎 Cinnamon powder
🌿 Kasuri methi
🍬 Sweetener, to taste
💧 Water, as required

How to Make –

1. Heat a pan and add cumin seeds, whole black peppercorns, green cardamom and bay leaf. Let them splutter.

2. Add the minced garlic, green chillies and melon seeds. Sauté for 1–2 minutes.

3. Add the chopped onion and cook until soft and lightly golden.

4. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they become completely soft and mushy.

5. Add salt, red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala and cinnamon powder. Cook the masala well.

6. Add the boiled cauliflower, boiled pumpkin and 100g paneer. Blend everything until completely smooth.

7. Pass the blended gravy through a sieve and pour it back into the pan.

8. Add 50ml low-fat milk and let the gravy simmer for 2–3 minutes.

9. Add the paneer cubes and cook for another 10 minutes so they absorb the flavours.

10. Stir in a little sweetener, crush kasuri methi between your palms, sprinkle it over the curry and serve hot.

reels.caption:
If you’re still convinced oats are boring, this Carrot Cake Oats recipe is here to change your mind. 🥕🥣

It tastes like cake, is gluten-free, gut-friendly, packs 18g protein + 7g fibre, and has officially earned permanent breakfast status in my kitchen.

✨ Recipe

• 50g Quaker Oats
• 50g grated carrot
• Water (as needed)
• Cinnamon (to taste)
• Nutmeg (to taste)
• 3 egg whites
• Vanilla extract (to taste)

Optional toppings:
Walnuts • Raisins • Banana • Extra cinnamon

Method:

1. Add oats, cinnamon, nutmeg, grated carrot and water to a pan.
2. Cook until the oats are almost done.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the 3 egg whites.
4. This step matters: Only add the egg whites when the oats are semi-cooked/almost cooked. Then whisk continuously for 2–3 minutes. Trust the process. The egg whites disappear completely and the oats become extra thick, creamy and high in protein. (If you add them too early or don’t whisk enough, you’ll end up with scrambled eggs instead of creamy oats. 😅)
5. Stir in vanilla, top with your favourites, and enjoy.

#AD #Quaker #QuakerIndia #collab #partnership

Recipe ⬇️ (35g Protein, 470 Cals) 

Ingredients (Makes 1 Sandwich) - 

🥒 9 thin slices of yellow zucchini
🥒 9 thin slices of green zucchini
🧀 60-70g low-fat paneer, grated
🧀 50–60g mozzarella cheese, grated

For the Filling 
🥔 Aloo Masala (optional)
- ½ potato medium size
-1 tsp jeera (cumin seeds)
-1 tsp rai (mustard seeds)
- 8–10 curry leaves
- 1 tsp red chilli powder
- ½ tsp coriander powder
- Salt, to taste

Assembly - 
🥒 Cucumber slices
🧅 Onion slices
🍅 Tomato slices
🩷 Beetroot slices
🌿 ½ tbsp green chutney
🌶️ 1/2 tbsp schezwan chutney

How to Make –

1. Heat a non-stick pan. Sprinkle grated mozzarella and low-fat paneer in a square shape. 
2. Arrange the zucchini slices on top of it, slightly overlapping.
3. Then add another thin layer of cheese and paneer on top.
4. Cook until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, then carefully flip and cook the other side.
5. Let both zucchini slices cool for a few minutes so they become firm before assembling.
6. Spread ½ tbsp green chutney on one slice, then layer the aloo masala, cucumber, onion, tomato, and beetroot.
7. Place the second zucchini slice on top.
8. Please wrap it up and then cut the sandwich into slices or the fillings will explode. 
9. Top with sev if feeling fancy❤️

Recipe ⬇️ (~80 Cals each)

Ingredients (Makes 12-15 Fudge Balls)

🥜 1/2 cup almonds
🌾 ¼ cup flax seeds
🎃 ¼ cup pumpkin seeds
🌴 120g soft dates (about 10–12 dates), pitted
🍫 2 tbsp cocoa powder
🧂 Pinch of salt
✨ Pinch of cinnamon
⚪ Roasted sesame seeds (for coating)
🥥 Roasted desiccated coconut (for coating)

How to Make -

1. Roast the almonds, flax seeds and pumpkin seeds until they turn lightly golden.
2. Add the roasted nuts and seeds to a blender along with the salt and cinnamon. Blend until the mixture reaches a thick, buttery consistency.
3. Add the dates and cocoa powder, then blend again until a sticky dough forms.
4. Roll the mixture into 22 equal-sized fudge balls.
5. Coat each ball in the roasted sesame seeds, roasted desiccated coconut, or a mix of both.
6. Refrigerate for 20–30 minutes and enjoy your healthy chocolate fudge balls! 🤎✨

I’ve also been making almonds a part of my daily routine by consuming them regularly and applying almond oil consistently pre hair wash. Hair has never felt this smooooooth✨🌸

Salt to taste

🌸Mix Greek yogurt and chilli sauce to make a quick creamy sauce.
🌸In another bowl, mix tomato, coriander, lemon juice, ketchup, and salt to make the salsa.

reels.caption:
Recipe🔽 (30g Protein - Kebabs + Greek Yogurt Dip)

1. Boil 35g of Soya Chunks and properly squeeze them to drain out all the water
2. In a kadhai, add 1 tsp ghee, 1 tsp jeera, 2-3 cloves chopped garlic and 2 chopped chillies
3. Then add 1 small chopped onion. Let it cook for 2 mins and add 1 cup fresh peas (incase you use frozen peas, soak in lukewarm water for a while).
4. Let the peas cook for 5 minutes and then add salt, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp aamchur, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp coriander powder, pinch of haldi and some rock salt.
5. Mix well and then add a tbsp of rice flour. Mix again and transfer this to a grinder jar. Add 1/2 slice of bread and handful of coriander and grind this mixture into a fine paste.
6. To this, add the soya chunks and grind again
7. Now keep this paste in the fridge for 10 minutes and apply oil on your hands and start making small balls.
8. On a non stick pan, brush some ghee and cook this kebabs on low-medium flame for a few minutes and until they have this beautiful brown color.
9. Serve with greek yogurt for more protein. Top the yogurt with red chilli powder, chaat masala and pomegranate (my star ingredient which goes so well with these)

1️⃣𝐄𝐚𝐭 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐬𝐞𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐬
You don't need to eat 1200 calories to see results. Sure, you would lose a huge amount of weight quickly, but that diet is highly unsustainable in the long run. Eat in a slight/moderate calorie deficit (200-500) and have 1.5-2.2 g of protein per kg of bodyweight. This is a slower but sustainable approach. 

2️⃣𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐨 𝐢𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚 𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐟𝐚𝐭 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐬
If you don't like cardio and you think you MUST do it to LOSE FAT, then that's not true. Find a form of exercise that you like doing and can continue doing in the long run. However, I want you add some walking to your day. This is the most underrated thing when it comes to fat loss. A 10 min walk after each meal will go a long way plus help you burn some extra calories on a deficit.

3️⃣𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐃𝐨 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐄𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐥 𝐁𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐬
Focus on quality rather than "how long you worked out" or "how many calories you burnt" or "if you had a sweaty session". Focus on improving your performance, mastering your technique, lifting heavier and progressive overload. Also, you don't need to workout 6-7 days a week. Even if you train 3-5 times a week, you would get similar infact better results. Make sure to train every muscle group twice in a week.
